title: Philosophical research and writing
stage: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
audience: a philosophy graduate preparing for doctoral study and research in metaphysics, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD
purpose: Learn the craft of professional philosophy: finding and reading the literature with PhilPapers and the encyclopedias, reconstructing the argument of a journal article, finding an original contribution, structuring and writing a paper, citation and academic integrity, refereeing, revising, presenting at conferences, and preparing a writing sample for graduate applications.
primary_reading: PhilPapers: the index of philosophical research (free)

weeks.1: What makes a philosophy paper good
weeks.2: Finding and reading the literature: PhilPapers, the encyclopedias and journals
weeks.11: Presenting at conferences and handling questions

blocks.deliverable: Build an annotated bibliography of ten sources.
Write a one-page reconstruction of a recent article.
Draft a thesis and an outline.
Week 7 midterm; submit a full first draft.
Write a referee report on a peer's draft.
Submit a revised paper and a 20-minute talk.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Writing sample: write and revise a 6,000- to 8,000-word paper in metaphysics with an original thesis, an accurate survey of the relevant literature and replies to the strongest objections; write a referee report on one peer paper; and prepare a 20-minute conference presentation of your own paper.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
